why: A reader that knows one lockfile format passes the others silently, and the four formats write the version four ways: package-lock v1 nests a version under each name, yarn v1 writes version "x", berry writes version: x, and pnpm puts it in the key (/name@x in v6, name@x in v9). Each project pins a different hijacked release in a different format, and each is confirmed.

files.code/b/yarn.lock:
# THIS IS AN AUTOGENERATED FILE. DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE DIRECTLY.
# yarn lockfile v1


cdeops@^13.5.0:
  version "13.5.31"
  resolved "https://registry.yarnpkg.com/cdeops/-/cdeops-13.5.31.tgz"
files.code/d/pnpm-lock.yaml:
lockfileVersion: '6.0'

dependencies:
  '@cdmbase/wiki-browser':
    specifier: ^12.0.0
    version: 12.0.18-alpha.53

packages:

  /@cdmbase/wiki-browser@12.0.18-alpha.53:
    resolution: {integrity: sha512-x}
    dev: false
